item.title: Steeped in bad economics
Sundarbans regains vibrancy after three-month closure
item.description:
The Sundarbans has regained its vibrancy after a three-month closure, with thousands of fishermen returning to its rivers and canals and tourists once again flocking to the world’s largest mangrove forest.
The 91-day ban on the entry of tourists and forest-dependent communities, imposed to protect biodiversity and ensure the breeding of wildlife and aquatic species, ended on August 31. The forest was reopened on September 1.
In the first six days after reopening, 36 tourist launches carrying 2,520 visitors, including eight foreign nationals, entered the Sundarbans, according to Forest Department officials. During the same period, 5,844 boats received boat licence certificates (BLCs) to enter the forest for fishing and crab collection.
The Sundarbans has 14 designated tourist spots under its eastern and western forest divisions. Every year, several lakh tourists visit the forest, while thousands of forest-dependent people enter with permission to collect fish, crabs, golpata and honey.
Since 2021, Forest Department has imposed the annual closure during the breeding season to minimize human disturbance and protect the forest’s biodiversity.
The reopening has already brought renewed activity to popular tourist destinations, particularly Karamjal in Bagerhat. Tourist vessels are regularly arriving at the jetty, while visitors are exploring foot trails and travelling to destinations, including Katka, Kochikhali, Jamtala and Andharmanik.
Visitors are arriving with family members, friends and organised groups to experience the forest’s rivers, canals and wildlife. Many are seen taking photographs and videos of deer, monkeys and other animals.
Karamjal Wildlife Breeding Centre officer-in-charge Hawlader Azad Kabir said tourist numbers were initially lower due to adverse weather but had been increasing as conditions improved. “We have taken necessary measures to ensure that tourists can visit safely and comfortably,” he said, urging visitors to act responsibly to help protect the fragile ecosystem.
Sundarbans East Division Divisional Forest Officer Md Rezaul Karim Chowdhury said the three-month closure had produced visible benefits for the forest and its wildlife. “During the closure, we observed a significant increase in the presence of fish in different canals. Wildlife also moved more freely,” he said.
He added that large herds of deer and tigers had been spotted during the closure, while several wildlife sightings were captured by Forest Department personnel.
Forest officials said the closure allowed wildlife to move with fewer disturbances. Tigers, crocodiles, deer, wild boars and monkeys were seen at different locations during the three-month period.
Sharankhola Range Assistant Conservator of Forests Md Shariful Islam said surveillance and patrols had been strengthened during the closure to prevent forest crimes and illegal entry. “Smart patrols were conducted for 20 days a month instead of the usual seven days, while patrol teams remained active round the clock depending on the tides,” he said.
Forest officials believe the return of tourists and fishermen, alongside increased sightings of wildlife and fish, reflects the positive impact of the three-month closure on the Sundarbans ecosystem.

item.title: Floating rafts open new prospects for mussel, coral fish farming in Cox’s Bazar
item.description:
Floating rafts have opened up new opportunities for green mussel and high-value coral fish farming in Cox’s Bazar, offering coastal communities an alternative source of income while creating fresh prospects for the country’s blue economy.
An experimental farm has been established near the mouth of the Bakkhali River in Sadar upazila of Cox’s Bazar, where local farmers are cultivating green mussels and coral fish using simple and environment-friendly technology.
The floating structures are made of bamboo, ropes and plastic drums. Mussel seeds are suspended beneath the rafts, allowing them to grow naturally in saline water. The mussels benefit from tidal flows and favorable coastal conditions, requiring little additional technology.
Project officials said mussels generally become suitable for harvesting within a few months. With demand for nutritious marine food increasing in Bangladesh, they believe commercial-scale production could meet domestic demand and eventually create opportunities for exports.
At the same time, high-value coral fish are being raised in large net cages attached to floating rafts. Fish fry is released into the cages and reared with regular feeding and care until they reach marketable size.
As coral fish fetch relatively high prices in local markets, farmers see considerable potential for generating profits from the venture.
Anwar Mia, a green mussel farmer, said he began cultivating green mussels on floating rafts in 2018 and has since been making profits from the initiative. “Floating mussel farming has been successful and has created an additional source of income alongside fishing,” he said.
He said such farms could become particularly important during periods when fishermen are unable to go to sea because of bad weather or seasonal fishing bans.
Another farmer, Shahidul Islam Babu, said fishing had previously been their main source of income. “When bad weather struck or fishing was banned, our income stopped. Now we are earning regularly by farming mussels and coral fish on floating rafts,” he said.
“With proper training and government support, this farming can be expanded on a larger scale,” he added.
Local farmer Mong Chen said he was initially hesitant about adopting the new technology but gained confidence after receiving training and technical assistance from the Integrated Development Foundation (IDF).
“The market price is good, and our family’s financial condition has improved. If farmers receive loans on easier terms and support with marketing, many more entrepreneurs will become interested in this sector,” he said.
The project is funded by Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) and implemented by Integrated Development Foundation (IDF). It provides local farmers with training, technical assistance and capacity-building support on modern marine aquaculture techniques.
Mohammad Hasan, an IDF fisheries officer, said the prospects for green mussel and marine fish farming on floating rafts in Bangladesh were very promising. “Coastal areas have abundant saline water and favorable environmental conditions, allowing the sector to expand rapidly,” he said.
Hasan said coordinated support from the government, research institutions and private organisations could turn floating aquaculture into a profitable and sustainable livelihood for coastal communities.
He said the initiative could also contribute to Bangladesh’s blue economy by making better use of the country’s extensive coastline and marine resources. “It can contribute to food security, create employment and generate foreign exchange,” he said.

item.title: August hottest month ever recorded globally
item.description:
The EU's climate monitor said Thursday that August was the hottest single month ever recorded globally, with ocean temperatures also reaching unprecedented highs as western Europe capped its warmest summer.
In response to the assessment by the Copernicus Climate Change Service, the UN warned that until humanity weaned off fossil fuels, the planet would only push deeper into uncharted territory.
Copernicus observations go back to 1940 but other evidence -- such as ice cores, tree rings and coral skeletons -- allow scientists to place today's climate against a much longer historical context.
“Humans haven't seen temperatures as hot as today for, arguably, at least the last 100,000 years,” Samantha Burgess from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which oversees Copernicus, told AFP.
Global average air temperatures in August were 16.96C, Copernicus said -- surpassing by 0.01°C the previous all-time monthly record set in July 2023. Copernicus said it considered the two months joint-highest given the narrow difference.
Scientists say that human activity -- primarily the burning of coal, oil and gas -- has warmed the planet by roughly 1.4°C since pre-industrial times and increased the severity and likelihood of extreme weather.
Yet heat-trapping greenhouse gas emissions rose to new highs in 2025.
“The evidence is irrefutable: this is the spiralling price of humanity's fossil fuel addiction, and the global climate crisis it is fueling,” United Nations climate chief Simon Stiell said of the Copernicus report.
Global sea surface temperatures also set a new daily high and tied equal-hottest for August, extending a three-month streak of record-breaking warmth across the world's oceans.
More than 90% of excess heat trapped by greenhouse gas emissions has been absorbed by the oceans, sparing land from warming but at severe cost to marine life, reefs and coastal communities.
Records tumbled in overheated basins like the Atlantic and Mediterranean and also the tropical Pacific, where the strongest El Nino weather pattern in the modern era is fast accumulating strength.
These events are marked by unusually warm Pacific waters but raise the odds of wild weather thousands of miles away, from floods in Peru to droughts in Africa and wildfires in Australia.
The warmer phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino episodes usually deliver a temporary spike in global temperatures already elevated by long-term background warming.
Scientists expect records to keep falling in the months ahead as this “super” El Nino approaches peak intensity around December and for 2027 -- and maybe even 2026 -- to become the hottest years ever observed.
“Climate change makes every El Nino hotter, and until we stop burning coal, oil, and gas these record-shattering months will simply keep on coming,” said Friederike Otto, a climate scientist from Imperial College London.
Copernicus also said that August “marked the end of western Europe's warmest summer” that surpassed the long-standing record set in 2003.
The June to August season was defined by severe, back-to-back heatwaves that shut schools, dried up rivers and primed the land for devastating wildfires.
Between mid-July and mid-August, the continent's EuroMomo monitoring platform estimated that Europe saw more than 32,000 excess deaths.
Scientists from the World Weather Attribution network concluded that a particularly strong heatwave in June would have been “virtually impossible” without the influence of climate change.
But extraordinary heat was felt around the globe.
On Wednesday, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration said the contiguous United States has endured its hottest summer on record.
And regions home to around 900 million people lived through the hottest July ever observed, according to AFP analysis of Copernicus data.
“We've had an exceptional summer -- not only in Europe, but other parts of the world where records that have existed for close to a century have fallen,” said Burgess, an ocean scientist and strategic lead for at ECMWF.
The climate would “continue to get more extreme unless we turn off the tap to global emissions,” she added.

Five people have been arrested in connection with a gunfight over an alleged drug trade in the Koratitola area of Gandaria in the capital, which left three people, including a woman, injured.
The arrestees are Mohammad Jisan, 19, Mohammad Ramzan, 19, Mohammad Shaheen, 34, Shabab Hossain Shaikat, 29, and Mohammad Mahim, 18.
The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB)-10 also recovered two foreign-made pistols, 12 rounds of ammunition, three magazines, and narcotics during the drives.

A gunfight took place between the Monir group and Auto Sajal group in Koratitola on Aug 30 over control of the drug trade, leaving passers-by Asha Akter, 20, and Siam, 18, and tea-stall owner Alamgir Hossain Rasel injured.
The RAB official said Alamgir and Siam have undergone surgery and are now recovering, while Asha is also stable. The bullet lodged in her leg, however, could not yet be removed.
Following the incident, a team of RAB-10's Jatrabari camp launched a shadow investigation.
The team identified those involved after analysing CCTV footage from the scene and surrounding areas along with intelligence information, RAB said.
On September 1, Jisan and Ramzan were arrested from the Munshiretek area of Gandaria around 7:30pm while Shaheen was arrested later on Sept 8.

RAB said two foreign-made pistols, 12 rounds of ammunition and three magazines were recovered from Shabab. Besides, 420 yaba pills valued at Tk3.13 lakh, 400 packets of heroin, 900 grams of cannabis and cash were recovered.

item.title: Safeguarding leadership summit to focus on child protection in Bangladesh
item.description:
Haileybury Bhaluka, in partnership with Cambridge University Press & Assessment, will host the Safeguarding Leadership Summit 2026 on Wednesday, September 16, at the Sky Ballroom of Le Méridien Dhaka.
The summit will bring together senior policymakers, school leaders, educators and safeguarding practitioners to discuss child protection and safeguarding standards across Bangladesh’s education sector.
Bobby Hajjaj, State Minister of Primary and Mass Education, will attend the summit as chief guest.
The summit is supported by international safeguarding organizations and will feature discussions on standards, frameworks and practices relevant to child protection in Bangladesh.
Cambridge University Press & Assessment is convening the event, drawing on its engagement with schools, educators and policymakers in Bangladesh. Its local team has helped shape the summit agenda, with a focus on applying international safeguarding standards to the local education context.
The summit is being led by Simon O’Grady, who has worked to raise awareness of safeguarding within Bangladesh’s schools. The event will focus on practical strategies for strengthening child protection policies, staff training and reporting systems.
O’Grady said: “This summit is about ensuring that every child in every school in Bangladesh grows up in an environment where their safety and wellbeing come first.”
He added: “By bringing together government, international expertise and school leadership under one roof, we hope to accelerate a genuine, nationwide culture of safeguarding.”

item.title: Yemen rebels report about 40 Saudi strikes in fresh attack
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels reported about 40 airstrikes launched by Saudi forces on Thursday in a fresh salvo following attacks by the Iran-backed group against the kingdom.
“The Saudi enemy’s air force conducted around 40 strikes in recent hours in the governorates of Taiz, Hodeida, Al-Jawf and Marib,” Houthi news agency Saba said.
The Houthis, who control large parts of northwest Yemen, launched a large-scale offensive last week against Yemeni government forces, who are backed by Saudi Arabia.
They also launched attacks on Saudi territory that left dozens wounded.
On Wednesday the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said the rebels fired ballistic missiles and drones at several cities in southern Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi civil defense issued alerts warning of “potential danger” in two areas, Khamis Mushait and Abha.
The Houthis are seeking to advance towards coastal areas of the Red Sea that border the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key shipping lane.
The waterway, which links Asia to Europe via the Red Sea and Suez Canal, has gained importance as a transit route since the start of the wider Middle East war, which saw Iran blockade the Strait of Hormuz.
Since last week, the fighting in Yemen has left more than 500 dead, mostly combatants, according to an AFP tally compiled from several sources.
The country relapsed into war in July after years of calm, drawn into the regional conflict triggered by the US-Israeli offensive against Iran that began at the end of February.

item.title: North Korea leader’s daughter believed to have younger sibling
item.description:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s daughter and apparent successor is believed to have a younger sibling, South Korea’s spy agency said on Thursday, offering a more detailed view of the ruling family’s line of succession.
Seoul’s spy agency has previously said Kim is thought to have three children, but some uncertainty remains on the number of offspring as well as the order of their birth.
The Kim dynasty is now in its third generation ruling the closed-off nation, and the current leader’s children would be potentially poised to take over one day.
Kim’s daughter, Kim Ju Ae, was first introduced to the public in 2022 when she accompanied her father to the launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile.
Seoul had initially indicated that Kim and his wife Ri Sol Ju had their first child, a boy, in 2010, and that Kim Ju Ae was their second child.
But in 2023, Seoul’s unification minister said that the government was “unable to confirm” the existence of the son.
The child described Thursday by South Korea’s spy agency would be the youngest.
“The National Intelligence Service currently assesses that Kim Ju Ae is being groomed as the successor and understands she has a younger sibling of unknown gender,” the agency said, reaffirming its conclusion on succession.
North Korea tightly controls information about its leadership and ruling family, leaving even basic details about Kim Jong Un’s children difficult to verify.
The NIS added that it was continuing to examine whether Kim Ju Ae has an older brother, but believes that “even if he exists, he is not in a position to become the successor.”
The age or even the gender of the children could be secondary to their potential as successors to their father, Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University, told AFP.
“Kim himself inherited power as the third-generation leader despite not being the eldest son,” he noted.
“In the same context, he would consider which of his children has the greatest potential to carry on his legacy and further develop his achievements,” Lim said.
“So we can assume that he assessed Ju Ae as having the greatest potential to become his successor,” he added.
Since 2022, Ju Ae has appeared at a number of major political events with the North Korean leader, including a high-profile visit to Beijing.
North Korean state media have also referred to her as “the beloved child” and a “great person of guidance” -- “hyangdo” in Korean -- a term typically reserved for top leaders and their successors.
Before 2022, the only confirmation of her existence had come from former NBA star Dennis Rodman, who reportedly made several visits to the North between 2013 and 2017.
Kim Ju Ae has drawn attention for her taste in luxury fashion, appearing in Gucci sunglasses and wearing a Cartier watch.
At other times, she has mirrored her father’s distinctive style, wearing matching leather jackets and dark glasses.

item.title: Wars pose a test as India hosts BRICS summit with Russia, Iran leaders
item.description:
India will host leaders including the presidents of Russia and Iran for a BRICS summit on Saturday, with wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, as well as economic challenges, to dominate talks among the 11-member group.
Vladimir Putin and his Iranian counterpart, Masoud Pezeshkian, are expected to arrive in New Delhi as early as Friday, with both due to hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has also been invited, although his participation in the two-day BRICS meeting has yet to be confirmed by Beijing.
It would be his first visit to India since 2019 -- and would mark the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the rival neighbors, six years after a deadly military clash along their disputed Himalayan border.
Ties between the nuclear-armed Asian giants have been warming since a deadly 2020 border clash, with flights, visas and high-level contacts gradually being restored.
However, deep mistrust remains, with their contested frontier, a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry still complicating ties.
“An India-China bilateral would be very important -- if it takes place,” said Pradeep Taneja, a China-India expert at the University of Melbourne.
Posters of a beaming Modi line streets across New Delhi to welcome leaders, with heavy deployments of security forces across the capital and widespread traffic restrictions in central districts.
Delhi police have urged people to “stay patient, stay cooperative,” with Friday declared a city holiday.
BRICS was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers.
It has since expanded and now includes Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates -- three countries with sharply differing positions on the war launched by the United States and Israel in February.
“The Gulf conflict is going to be the central fault line this time during the BRICS summit,” said Harsh V. Pant of India’s Observer Research Foundation.
“What was seen until last year as an achievement -- the expansion of BRICS -- today looks like a big constraint on BRICS,” Pant said.
It will be Pezeshkian’s first visit to India as president, and will put the Middle East conflict firmly on the agenda.
“The war in Iran will provide a stern test of the (expanded) group’s cohesion,” said Shilan Shah of Capital Economics, noting the failure of the BRICS foreign ministers to agree on a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May.
India maintains cordial relations with Iran and Israel, but is also careful to strike a delicate balance in its ties with Washington.
India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the Iran war in part by turning to Russia, one of its most important strategic partners and its most controversial fuel supplier in recent years as the war with Ukraine drags on.
Putin last visited India in December 2025, but he also met Modi in Bishkek this month.
Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar visited Kyiv this month, when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was “grateful to India for its commitment to ending this unjust war.”

item.title: Philippine ferry fire kills 5, dozens missing
item.description:
Philippine rescuers raced on Thursday to extinguish a fire that erupted aboard a ferry near a tourist hotspot, killing at least five people and leaving 86 others missing, according to the coast guard.
The blaze broke out on the M/V June Aster Wednesday evening about 2.2 kilometers (1.3 miles) off the coast of Palawan province, the coast guard said, adding that five bodies as well as 43 survivors had been brought ashore.
The coast guard has yet to establish the cause of the fire, but said one survivor reported hearing a “loud explosion” from the cargo hold.
“After that there was smoke and fire. As per the testimony of the survivor, it escalated quickly. After seconds, the fire started spreading,” Coast Guard spokeswoman Noemie Cayabyab told reporters Thursday.
With the fire not yet extinguished, rescuers have been unable to search the vessel, Cayabyab said, adding that some people may still be trapped inside.
Waiting for nearly 24 hours for updates about the missing, hundreds of people desperate for news about the incident have left comments on the Facebook page of a local mayor, searching for relatives, friends and even a dog.
The ferry’s manifest listed 134 passengers and crew. Of the 43 rescued, 38 were passengers and four were crew, said Cayabyab. The identity of another survivor was not immediately clear.
“Most of the people we rescued were those who had been swimming away from the vessel,” said the spokeswoman.
She said many were in a state of shock, and comprehensive interviews that could shed light on the incident will only take place later on.
As the search continued for the 86 people presumed missing, coast guard, military personnel and local responders were working to tamp down the thick smoke billowing from the ferry.
The ferry, which left from the capital Manila and was headed for the town of Coron, is currently aground on an island in Palawan province.
In January, a triple-decker ferry carrying more than 340 people sank off the southern Philippines, killing at least 52 people.
The M/V Trisha Kerstin 3 sank along nearly the same route where 31 people died in 2023 after a fire broke out aboard the Lady Mary Joy 3 ferry.

item.title: Social Welfare Minister: Tech-driven industries like Walton key to advancing 4IR
item.description:
Social Welfare Minister Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain has said that Walton is manufacturing high-tech electronics and electrical products, including refrigerators and televisions, as well as high-configuration laptops and tablets. The company manufactures everything from components and parts to fully finished products.
“Walton products offer superior quality and durability at affordable prices. Alongside creating significant employment opportunities, Walton is also helping the country save substantial foreign currency through local production of technology products,” he said.
The minister made the remarks while visiting Walton Headquarters at Chandra in Gazipur on Tuesday (September 8).
During the visit, he witnessed the manufacturing processes of various world-class, high-tech products, solar power facilities and environmentally sustainable production practices at Walton Headquarters.
The minister expressed his admiration after gaining first-hand insights into Bangladesh’s progress in electrical, electronics and high-tech manufacturing, technological capabilities and export activities.
Upon his arrival at Walton Headquarters, the minister was welcomed with flowers by Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC’s directors SM Rezaul Alam and SM Monjurul Alam Ovee.
The minister began his visit by watching a video documentary highlighting the manufacturing processes of various Walton products.
He then toured the display centre showcasing a wide range of technology products manufactured by Walton.
Later, he visited different manufacturing facilities, including the PCB or motherboard production plant equipped with state-of-the-art SMT (Surface Mount Technology) machines.
He also visited the country’s largest floating solar power plant installed at Walton Headquarters and learned about the company’s technological excellence, quality control, research and development, and export activities.
Following the visit, the minister said: “I previously had mixed perceptions about Walton. I used to think that Walton perhaps only assembled or reassembled products. But after visiting the factory today, my perception has completely changed. I am truly impressed.”
Praising Walton’s environmentally sustainable manufacturing practices, he said: “Walton is using renewable energy, which is a very good initiative.”
Highlighting the importance of technology-driven industries to the national economy, the minister said: “We have reached a certain level of advancement in agriculture and the ready-made garment sector. To move forward in the era of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, we now need to accelerate the growth of technology-driven industries like Walton.”
“The present government is committed to supporting local industries. The growth and development of domestic industries will create more employment opportunities,” he added.
The minister further said: “To support domestic industrialization, the government has provided tax and policy support in the national budget for FY2026-27. Our all-out support for the growth of local industries will continue.”

PSG thrash Slovan in Champions League opener, Liverpool down Atletico
item.description:
Holders Paris Saint-Germain made a smooth start to their bid for a third consecutive Champions League title as Ferran Torres scored a hat-trick in a 6-1 rout of Slovan Bratislava on Wednesday, while Liverpool came from behind to beat Atletico Madrid.
Barcelona kicked off their campaign by scoring five goals against Feyenoord, while Arsenal impressed with a 1-0 win at Napoli.
PSG, who are hoping to become only the fourth club to win three European Cups in a row, visit Manchester City and host Barca in their next two European games.
"It is the Champions League, we always play against tough teams, but we have to be focused first in Ligue 1 because we didn't start in the right way," said Torres, with PSG yet to win a domestic game this season.
But they wasted little time in picking apart Yaya Toure's Slovan at the Parc des Princes.
Ousmane Dembele hammered in a rebound and then nodded in a deflected cross to put Luis Enrique's men two goals ahead inside 22 minutes.
Torres tapped home Dembele's cross just after the half-hour mark and drilled in his second less than two minutes after the restart.
Spain's World Cup final hero completed his hat-trick in the 57th minute, shanking a shot with his knee that spun into the bottom corner.
Suleiman Camara crashed in a consolation for Slovan, but Fabian Ruiz had the final say for PSG when he pounced on a mishit clearance.
Liverpool made it successive victories after winning at Ipswich in the Premier League last week by beating Atletico 2-1 at Anfield.
Atletico grabbed a 17th-minute lead as Julian Alvarez, starting for the first time this season after failing to force a move away from the club, played in Marcos Llorente to dink the ball over Alisson in the Liverpool goal.
Llorente has now scored five times in three visits to Anfield, after netting a double at Liverpool last season and in Atletico's dramatic last-16 victory in 2020.
Liverpool hit back five minutes before the break through Dominik Szoboszlai, courtesy of a clever backheeled pass from Ronald Araujo.
Alexis Mac Allister then hammered the hosts in front five minutes into the second half with a left-footed strike from outside the box, and Atletico could not find a response.
"I've loved it. The atmosphere has been incredible and I feel lucky, lucky to experience it," said Liverpool's new manager Andoni Iraola after his Champions League coaching debut.
Arsenal missed several first-half chances at the Stadio Armando Diego Maradona, with Napoli goalkeeper Alex Meret making an excellent save to keep out Mikel Merino's header.
Piero Hincapie fired over a golden chance from just three yards out as the English champions continued to push after half-time, but last season's runners-up finally forged ahead with 15 minutes left.
Martin Odegaard, who scored the winner against Chelsea at the weekend, played a clever one-two with Christos Tzolis on the edge of the area and crashed a shot in off the far post.
Barcelona made an excellent start to their latest bid to end a 12-year wait to lift the trophy, as Raphinha continued his superb form by scoring twice in a 5-1 thumping of Feyenoord.
Hansi Flick's men, who lost to Atletico in the quarter-finals last season, have won all five of their matches in all competitions so far this season, scoring five goals in four of them.
"We controlled the game, we are dominant and this is fantastic to see. This is our style and how we want to play," said Flick.
Raphinha put Barca into a third-minute lead before a brilliant long-range strike from summer signing Karim Adeyemi.
Brazilian Raphinha, playing up front this season after the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Torres, made it eight goals already for the campaign in the second half.
Lamine Yamal netted a free-kick which crept through the wall, and although Sem Steijn pulled one back for Feyenoord, Gabriel Jesus came off the bench and then headed in his first Barca goal.
Ermedin Demirovic scored a first-half hat-trick as Stuttgart eased to a 3-1 home win over Norwegian champions Viking, playing in the competition for the first time in 34 years.
Sporting, quarter-finalists last season for the first time since 1983, fought back to see off Galatasaray 3-1 in Lisbon.

item.title: PM: Feasibility study, design completed for Chittagong-Dhaka electric train
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday said the government has completed the feasibility study and detailed design for introducing electric trains on Chittagong-Dhaka corridor to reduce travel time and improve connectivity between the two most important cities.
“The feasibility study and detailed design for installing electric traction to operate electric trains on the Chittagong-Dhaka corridor have already been completed,” he said while replying to a starred question from Chittagong-12 MP Mohammed Enamul Hoque during the question-answer session in parliament.
The prime minister said the detailed implementation plan and timeline for the project would be determined after securing the necessary financing.
“The project will be taken up for implementation subject to securing funding. Once implemented, electric trains can be operated on the Chittagong-Dhaka corridor, increasing the average speed of trains and reducing travel time,” he said.
Tarique also said a feasibility study and detailed design are underway for constructing a chord line from Dhaka to Comilla to shorten the distance between Dhaka and Chittagong.
“Once implemented, the distance between Dhaka and Chittagong will be reduced and the average speed will increase, allowing people to travel between the two cities in less time,” he said.
The government has also taken steps to convert the Dhaka-Chittagong railway into a dual-gauge double line, the prime minister said.
As part of the initiative, feasibility studies and detailed designs for constructing dual-gauge double lines on the Tongi-Akhaura and Laksam-Chittagong sections have already been completed.
Laksam-Chittagong Dual Gauge Double Line Development Project is currently being processed for approval, while preparation of the Development Project Proforma (DPP) for the Tongi-Akhaura project is at its final stage, the prime minister said.
“I hope that once these two projects are implemented, Bangladesh Railway’s passenger transport capacity and train speeds on the Chittagong-Dhaka corridor will increase,” he said.
The parliamentary session began at 3:30pm with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed in the chair.
The first half-hour of the session was allocated for the prime minister’s question-answer session.

item.title: Legal notice seeks mobile network services on Dhaka Metro Rail
item.description:
A legal notice has been sent to Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL), seeking steps to ensure uninterrupted mobile network and call services on metro rail and at stations in Dhaka.
Advocate H M Rashidul Islam Rashed, general secretary of the BUBT Lawyers Association (BULA), sent the notice in the public interest on Wednesday.
Addressed to the managing director of DMTCL, the notice asked the company to allow the country’s 3 major mobile operators — Grameenphone, Banglalink and Robi Axiata (Airtel) — to install mobile network infrastructure in metro rail areas and provide necessary infrastructural facilities.
According to the notice, around 400,000 passengers use the metro rail every day. However, weak or unavailable network services on moving trains and at stations prevent passengers from making emergency calls, while other calls may be disconnected.
The notice requested that necessary steps be taken within 15 days of receiving it and that the sender be informed in writing.
Otherwise, it said legal measures, including filing a writ petition before the High Court in the public interest, would be taken.

item.title: State minister: Dengue outbreak may peak by end of September
item.description:
State Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dr MA Muhit has said the ongoing dengue outbreak may peak in the last week of September and early October.
He made the remarks at a seminar marking World Suicide Prevention Day, organised by the Aachal Foundation and the Human Rights Development Centre, at Dhaka Reporters Unity on Wednesday.
Dr Muhit said dengue cases had started rising again and that the government had launched a three-month campaign to prevent the spread of the disease.
“We are currently facing an urgent public health issue—dengue. Dengue cases have risen again; the increase began yesterday. Two days ago, we predicted that the peak period would arrive in the last week of this month and early October,” he said.
“Prevention is key here. We held a meeting yesterday under the leadership of the prime minister, and we are launching a three-month campaign regarding dengue.”
He said the campaign would involve voluntary organisations and the public, with a focus on dengue prevention, cleanliness drives and raising awareness.
“By involving people and ensuring that everyone looks after their own homes and workplaces, we can protect ourselves, as well as the relatives we live with and the colleagues we work alongside, from dengue,” he said.
He added that the government was also emphasising cleanliness in urban areas as part of its dengue prevention efforts.
Regarding the government’s dengue response, Dr Muhit said there were two main objectives: reducing infections and lowering the mortality rate.
“To achieve this, we—along with the city corporations, Local Government and the Ministry of Health—are working together on prevention, cleaning operations and larvicide application,” he said.
He said steps had also been taken to reduce dengue-related deaths, including refresher training for doctors.
“Working in collaboration with the Society of Medicine, a standard management protocol was developed, and 300 doctors have already received training based on it,” he said.
“Yesterday, we held a meeting with civil surgeons from across the country. We will continue this training programme in every district and upazila nationwide.”
Dr Muhit said dengue outbreaks often cause sudden increases in patient numbers, resulting in shortages of hospital beds, saline and dengue testing kits.
“We began stockpiling supplies two months ago. Based on current trends, we have adequate stocks of dengue test kits and saline. We have also taken measures to ensure this supply chain remains uninterrupted in the future,” he said.
On dedicated dengue beds, he said hospitals had already been instructed to designate beds for dengue patients.
“Should the number of cases rise further, we can increase bed capacity during the peak season,” he said.
“At the same time, we have urged the private sector to step up and play a role during the dengue peak. They must not arbitrarily hike prices during this period and are required to maintain dedicated beds for dengue patients in their facilities.”

item.title: PM: Govt takes measures to prevent project delays, cost increases
item.description:
The government is taking steps to curb repeated extensions in the duration and cost of development projects, as concerns over prolonged implementation and rising expenses persist.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman disclosed the measures on Wednesday in reply to a written question from Comilla-10 lawmaker Md Mobasher Alam Bhuiyan during the question-answer session of the 3rd session of the 13th National Parliament.
The parliamentary session began at 3:30pm with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram in the chair. At the outset, the prime minister answered written questions.
Tarique said: “The extension of duration and increase in the cost of government development projects in Bangladesh usually do not occur for a single reason. Rather, multiple weaknesses in project formulation, approval, land acquisition, financing, procurement processes and management become interconnected to create this problem.”
He said: “After the government became aware of the tendency to extend project durations and increase costs, various measures have been taken in this regard. These include ensuring accurate feasibility studies before taking up new projects and initiatives to speed up implementation preparations after project approval.”
Work is underway to update the existing guidelines on project formulation, processing, approval and revision, he said. Dashboards are also being established in the relevant ministries and divisions to strengthen monitoring of ongoing projects.
Regular project reviews and close field-level monitoring have also been increased, he said.
Coordination among relevant agencies is being strengthened to expedite land acquisition and utility relocation work.
Instructions have been given to take action under the rules against individuals and organizations responsible for delays after reviewing the reasons for delays, irregularities, increased costs and revisions in projects not completed within the stipulated time, the prime minister said.
“For projects with implementation progress below 30%, the relevant ministries or divisions are taking appropriate measures regarding their restructuring, changes in scope or continuation after considering their utility and effectiveness,” he said.
“In addition, instructions have been given to take up cluster projects under integrated programs instead of taking up projects separately,” he added.
The prime minister also said the use of the electronic government procurement (e-GP) system in government procurement would be expanded.
In appointing project directors, professional qualifications, skills and practical experience will be given the highest priority, while initiatives have been taken to ensure continuity of responsibility where necessary. Work is underway to update the existing policy for this purpose, he said.
Instructions have also been given to prioritize taking up projects under the public-private partnership (PPP) model, Tarique told parliament.
An initiative has also been taken to update the Public Procurement Rules 2025 to make government procurement more competitive and accountable.

item.title: PM: Diesel-powered irrigation pumps to be replaced with solar system within 5yrs
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday said the government plans to gradually replace diesel-powered irrigation pumps with solar-powered systems across the country within the next five years.
Replying to a supplementary question from Meherpur-1 MP Md Tajuddin Khan during the prime minister’s question-answer session in parliament, Tarique said all diesel-powered water pumps would be brought under the solar power program in phases.
“Yes, the current government has this plan. Wherever water pumps are operated by diesel, we will gradually shift all of them to solar power within the next five years, Inshallah,” he said.
Tarique was responding to a question on whether the government planned to provide farmers with solar power free of cost for irrigation instead of diesel-powered engines.
In response to the mp’s starred question, the prime minister outlined the government’s broader plan to expand renewable energy, including solar power, to reduce dependence on imported fuel.
He said the government has set a target of meeting at least 20% of total electricity generation from renewable sources by 2030 and 30% by 2040.
The government has also set targets of generating 5,500MW from rooftop solar, 4,500MW from ground-mounted solar and 450-550MW from other renewable sources, including wind, waste-to-energy, hydropower, floating solar and agrivoltaics by 2030.
Replying to another supplementary question from reserved women’s seat-11 MP Nipun Roy Chowdhury, Tarique said the government was encouraging the use of lithium batteries for solar power storage and would support industries that manufacture them.
He said lead-acid batteries use acid that is harmful to the environment, while lithium batteries are more environmentally friendly.
“The government is trying to encourage lithium batteries. The government will provide all kinds of support to industries that will be established for manufacturing lithium batteries,” he said.
Tarique also indicated that the government might make lithium batteries mandatory for rooftop solar systems in the future.
The parliamentary session began at 3:30pm with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed in the chair.
The first half-hour was allocated for the prime minister’s question-answer session.

item.title: Yemen rebels report fresh Saudi strikes as conflict deepens
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels reported dozens of Saudi airstrikes on Wednesday as daily attacks continued in a conflict that has reignited during the Middle East war, with hundreds of people killed in fighting near the Red Sea.
More than 40 attacks targeted several regions including the flashpoint areas of Taiz and Hodeida, scene of fierce clashes between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government, the rebels said.
The latest salvos in Yemen’s previously dormant conflict come a day after the Iran-backed Houthis set oil sites ablaze and wounded 73 in their heaviest missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia in years.
The Yemen fighting is taking place against the backdrop of the Middle East war, which erupted in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
On Wednesday, Iran said it attacked 20 American vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and targeted a US military base in Jordan in retaliation for US strikes on Iranian oil tankers.
The Middle East war has sucked in Yemen, the energy-rich Gulf and others across the region while roiling the world economy, as oil prices returned to $100 a barrel on Wednesday.
More than 500 people have died since the Houthis launched a major offensive last week to seize territory around the Bab al-Mandab strait, gateway to the Red Sea shipping route.
The rebels, who have been attacking Saudi oil tankers, are trying to tighten their squeeze on the shipments, analysts say -- a lifeline for exports after Iran’s blockade of Hormuz.
Saudi airstrikes targeted “various areas across the governorates of Marib, Al-Jawf, Taiz and Hodeida over the past few hours,” the rebels’ Almasirah TV said on Wednesday.
There was no official comment from Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi civil defense later issued a warning for the southern governorate of Khamis Mushait, near Yemen, but quickly lifted it.
On Tuesday, Saudi authorities vowed to respond to the Houthi attacks, saying they caused fires and temporary shutdowns at oil sites.
The Houthis triggered the return to hostilities in July, when they let an Iranian plane land in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace.
The government retaliated by striking the airport, an attack the rebels blamed on its sponsor, Saudi Arabia.
The ongoing exchanges risk returning Yemen to a conflict that left hundreds of thousands of people dead and sparked one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.
The Houthis, after seizing Yemen’s capital and forcing out the internationally recognized government, fought a Saudi-led coalition from 2015 until a United Nations-brokered ceasefire in 2022.
On Tuesday, the European Union urged the Houthis to end their attacks, calling them a “dangerous escalation.”
“We call on the Houthis to immediately end all attacks inside and outside Yemen, including attacks against commercial shipping in the Red Sea,” said Anouar El Anouni, a spokesman for the bloc’s diplomatic service.

item.title: NCC Bank launches Bangla QR service
item.description:
NCC Bank has recently launched Bangla QR services at various selected retail merchant points across the country.
The primary objective of this initiative is to expand the scope of cashless and digital transactions nationwide and ensure easy, fast, and secure payment facilities for customers.
The bank's managing director M Shamsul Arefin inaugurated the service by distributing Bangla QR codes to approximately 200 retail merchants at Sonargaon Janopath Road, the Ceramic Market adjacent to Tongi Chirag Ali Bus Stand, and Savar New Market.
With the launch of this service, small traders, shop owners, and general consumers in those areas will be able to reduce their reliance on cash and make digital payments simply by scanning the QR code.
This will not only make transactions faster and safer but will also preserve a digital record of every transaction.
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Md Habibur Rahman, the bank’s deputy managing director; Mohammad Tariqul Amin, SEVP (corporate banking); AKM Jahidul Alam, EVP & head of operations; Md Jashimuddin, SVP & region head of Outskirt Dhaka; Sharif Mohammad Mahsin, SVP & head of SME; Md Sajjadul Islam, SVP & head of ICT; Md Anisur Rahman Majumder, VP & head of financial inclusion cell; SM Tanvir Hasan, head of retail business unit, DFS Business & Bangla QR, along with other senior officials of the bank.

item.title: Nepal Embassy in Dhaka opens donation account for flood victims
item.description:
The Embassy of Nepal in Dhaka has appealed to individuals, organisations and institutions in Bangladesh for voluntary financial contributions to support victims of the devastating August 26 flash floods, opening a dedicated bank account to channel assistance.
The appeal comes after the floods along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers caused widespread loss of life and property, leaving many people injured, missing and severely affected.
The August 26 disaster was triggered after a massive collapse of glacial ice and rock sent debris into the Lhende Khola, unleashing a destructive surge through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems and sweeping through settlements and critical infrastructure downstream.
As of Wednesday, 1,367 bodies had been recovered in Nepal, while 5,132 people remained officially listed as missing, including around 589 foreign tourists, according to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
Only 102 of the recovered bodies had so far been identified and handed over to their families.
In a notice issued on September 8 titled “Together for Nepal: An Appeal for Voluntary Contributions to Support Flash Flood Victims,” the embassy said it had received an outpouring of solidarity and offers of assistance from the Bangladesh government, members of the public, institutions and other friends and well-wishers of Nepal.
With inquiries growing over how people in Bangladesh could contribute to the relief effort, the embassy said it had established a dedicated account for voluntary donations.
“We invite interested individuals, organizations and institutions in Bangladesh to join hands with the people of Nepal in this time of need,” the embassy said.
“Every contribution, big or small, will be deeply appreciated.”
According to the notice, contributions can be deposited with Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC under the account name “Embassy of Nepal, Dhaka,” account number 1000028629, at its Gulshan branch.
The appeal adds a public fundraising channel to the assistance already extended by Bangladesh following the catastrophe.
The Bangladesh government earlier contributed $1 million to the Nepal Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund to support ongoing relief, recovery and humanitarian operations following the floods and landslides.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had also expressed condolences over the loss of life and offered Bangladesh’s assistance to Nepal, while the National Parliament adopted a condolence motion over the disaster.
The Nepal Embassy said the dedicated account was opened specifically in response to increasing requests from Bangladeshis seeking ways to help those affected.
The August 26 disaster caused extensive damage across northern Nepal, destroying homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure and leaving communities struggling with the consequences of one of the country’s most severe recent natural disasters.
The embassy said those seeking further information about making contributions could contact its designated officials.
The latest appeal now gives individuals and organisations in Bangladesh a direct avenue to join the government-level response and contribute to Nepal’s recovery effort.

item.title: Power, internet restored after fire at Rooppur
item.description:
Electricity and internet connections have been restored following a fire in a room at the Pioneer Base of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Project in Ishwardi, Pabna. Officials said normal operations at the project are continuing.
The fire broke out around 3am on Monday in the server room of the Pioneer Base, damaging several computers, air conditioners, documents, electrical equipment and internet server components.
An Ishwardi Fire Service unit responded and brought the fire under control. Officials said three additional units were also present as part of a routine fire service drill.
Following the fire, electricity supplies to two buildings, including the Pioneer Base, and internet connections to several project offices were temporarily disrupted. The disruption also caused a brief water shortage at the customs building and canteen, but services were later restored.
The fire service initially suspected that an electrical short circuit may have caused the fire. However, the exact cause will be determined after an investigation.
Abu Hashem, the senior station officer on duty at the site, said the fire occurred in a room outside the radiation zone.
“The fire was quickly brought under control, and electricity and internet services are now functioning normally,” he said.

item.title: EasyBuy.com.bd launches to simplify product sourcing from China
item.description:
EasyBuy.com.bd, a cross-border wholesale marketplace and sourcing platform, has officially launched with the aim of simplifying product sourcing from China for Bangladeshi entrepreneurs.
The platform was recently unveiled at a grand ceremony held at its corporate office in Elephant Road, Dhaka, under the slogan, “Source Easy, Grow Fast.”
EasyBuy.com.bd will enable entrepreneurs to search for and source a range of products from China at wholesale prices based on their business requirements.
For many aspiring entrepreneurs, students and professionals looking to start online or small-scale businesses, selecting suitable products, identifying suppliers and navigating the sourcing process in China can be challenging.
The platform aims to make these processes more accessible and streamlined.
“Our goal is to simplify the process of sourcing products from China, create new business opportunities for Bangladeshi entrepreneurs and help them grow their businesses,” said Kauser Khandoker, founder and managing director of EasyBuy.com.bd.
Mahsin Ali, co-founder of the company, said the platform seeks to help entrepreneurs source quality products more easily, allowing them to launch and expand their businesses.
EasyBuy.com.bd is an affiliate of Galaxy Cargo International, which has been operating in the China-Bangladesh trade and logistics sector since 2016.
The platform draws on the company's experience in cross-border trade and its network in China to support entrepreneurs throughout the sourcing process.
According to the company, it maintains its own warehouse and office in China, supported by local employees and a dedicated sourcing team that assists customers in identifying and procuring products.
EasyBuy.com.bd aims to serve existing small and medium-sized enterprises, as well as aspiring entrepreneurs, students, professionals and e-commerce businesses seeking easier access to products from China.

item.title: High Court: NID cannot be issued without photograph
item.description:
The High Court has dismissed a rule that sought to introduce an alternative system for issuing National Identity (NID) cards using biometric features instead of photographs.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Md Iqbal Kabir and Justice SM Saiful Islam delivered the verdict on Wednesday.
As a result, photographs will remain mandatory for obtaining an NID card.
Lawyers Sheikh Omar Sharif and Ilias Ali Mondal represented the petitioner, while lawyer Kamal Hossain Miyaji appeared for the Election Commission.
Confirming the verdict, Miyaji said the dismissal of the rule meant that NID cards could not be issued without photographs.
Sumaiya Ahmad Muna, a resident of Shantibagh in the capital's Shahjahanpur area, filed the writ petition in 2022, stating that she observes purdah in accordance with Islamic Sharia and therefore refrains from having her photograph taken.
Her husband, Muhammad Arifur Rahman, was authorized to act on her behalf in connection with the petition.
On February 10, 2022, Muna submitted an application to the Election Commission seeking an alternative method of obtaining an NID card without providing a photograph.
She said that as an adult Muslim woman who strictly observes purdah, she had been unable to obtain an NID card and was consequently being deprived of various services and benefits.
As her application remained unresolved, she filed a writ petition with the High Court.
Following a hearing, the High Court issued a rule on March 6, 2022, asking why the authorities should not be directed to take necessary steps to issue NID cards using alternative identification methods, including biometric features, without requiring photographs.
The High Court dismissed the rule on Wednesday.
During the initial hearing, state counsel argued that the petition itself was unconstitutional, noting that photographs are required for purposes including Hajj registration and opening bank accounts.
The state also argued that biometric identification could require iris scanning, which would involve lifting the veil.

item.title: Iran attacks US base in Jordan as Hormuz impasse deepens
item.description:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they pummeled a US military base in Jordan, vowing retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers that dragged the foes deeper into war.
Tehran's bombs came after US forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to Iran targeting an American warship, the second such attack in less than a week.
The United States and Iran are locked in a stalemate six months into the war, with Iran maintaining a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas, and Washington pushing a campaign to choke Iran's ports and economy.
The Islamic Republic said on Wednesday it would target oil tankers off US-allied Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for the strikes on its tankers.
Minutes later, Iran's Revolutionary Guards -- the most powerful arm of the Iranian military -- said they had struck the US air base of Al-Azraq in Jordan with missiles, state media reported.
The "punitive operation" damaged maintenance and repair facilities, deployment locations and shelters for fighter jets, according to IRNA.
Jordan's army said it shot down 18 missiles from Iran targeting the kingdom.
The strikes came after Tehran urged crews on oil tankers off Kuwait and Bahrain to leave their vessels, warning they "will be targeted", the Guards said in a statement posted on IRNA.
The latest flare-up was triggered after US forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers, with the US military saying it "directed the crews to abandon ship" before hitting the vessels.
"Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers, and I think you'll see that again today," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Tuesday on a visit to Colombia.
Iranian media reported Tuesday that a US missile struck a tanker off the coast of Kharg Island, adding that there were no casualties.
The chief of staff of Iran's army Ali Abdollahi had warned the Islamic republic would hit US bases in the region if Iranian oil tankers were hit.
Global oil prices climbed on Wednesday to near $100 a barrel as the war threatened to further choke supply from the crude-rich Middle East.
The price of Brent crude, the benchmark international contract, rose to $99.38 per barrel, while the main US contract West Texas Intermediate was at $94.51 per barrel.
Iran has largely controlled the Strait of Hormuz -- which normally carries around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas -- since the start of the war in February, with traffic through the waterway virtually paralysed.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards also said on Tuesday they seized "one of the most modern, unmanned" American submarine drone in the Strait of Hormuz.
The US military said that the drone had "malfunctioned", insisting it was an "older model" that did not carry any sensitive data.
Iranian state TV also said the Guards had attacked two US destroyers with ballistic missiles.
The US military did not immediately comment on the report.

item.title: Bangladesh braces for 2–3 heatwaves in September
item.description:
Bangladesh is likely to experience a warmer-than-usual September, with the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) forecasting two to three mild to moderate heatwaves across the country during the month.
According to the department’s long-range weather outlook, both daytime and nighttime temperatures are expected to remain above normal, raising the possibility of prolonged periods of hot and uncomfortable weather in several parts of the country.
The outlook was issued following a meeting of the Expert Team on Long-Range Weather Forecasting.
Assistant Meteorologist at the BMD Afruza Sultana said rainfall is likely to remain below normal across all divisions, suggesting that September could be comparatively drier and warmer than usual.
She said the country may experience two to three mild to moderate heatwaves during the month, with temperatures potentially rising to 36–37 degrees Celsius.
According to Sultana, Dhaka, Rajshahi and Khulna divisions are likely to experience the heat more intensely, with the central and western parts of the country expected to be among the areas most affected by the warmer conditions.
“Usually, moisture levels are higher during this time, causing people to sweat more and making it harder for sweat to dry quickly,” she said.
“As a result, people feel more uncomfortable than they do in April, even when temperatures rise above 38°C, because of the higher moisture in the air in September,” she said.
The combination of above-normal temperatures and below-normal rainfall could increase discomfort for residents and put additional pressure on water resources, particularly during prolonged dry spells, she said.
According to the BMD forecast, Dhaka is expected to receive around 260–270 mm of rainfall in September, while Rajshahi may record 240–270 mm and Chattogram 330–360 mm.
Although rain will remain possible, the overall rainfall totals are expected to stay slightly below the respective long-term averages.
Meteorologists have also warned that one to three low-pressure systems could develop over the Bay of Bengal during September. At least one of these systems may strengthen into a monsoon depression, potentially bringing periods of heavy rain to parts of the country.
Despite the overall drier outlook, localized flooding remains a possibility. Rising water levels in major rivers and monsoon rainfall could trigger short-term flooding, particularly in the northern, northeastern and southeastern regions.
Thunderstorms are also expected on around three to five days during the month.
The latest forecast follows a mixed rainfall pattern in August. Chittagong and Mymensingh received above-normal rainfall, while Rajshahi and Rangpur experienced significant rainfall deficits.
Four low-pressure systems formed over the Bay of Bengal during August, with two developing into monsoon depressions that produced heavy rain and thunderstorms.
The highest daily rainfall recorded last month was 198 mm in Hatiya, while the country’s highest temperature reached 37°C in Rajshahi.
With September expected to be comparatively warmer and drier, the BMD has urged residents, farmers and local authorities to remain prepared for heatwaves, water stress and sudden localized flooding as weather conditions evolve.

item.title: US destroys five Iran oil tankers after attacks on American warship
item.description:
US forces destroyed five Iranian oil carriers on Tuesday after Tehran launched ballistic missiles at an American warship twice in recent days, the US military said.
The strikes are the second time Washington has targeted Iranian tankers in less than a week in response to attacks on US military vessels, and Tehran vowed to hit back by targeting oil carriers near US-allied Gulf states.
"American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable," US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a statement on the strikes, which were "in response to Iran's most recent failed attacks."
The destruction of the tankers came after "the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days," CENTCOM said.
The warship "successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and continued to patrol regional waters," it said.
US forces destroyed three Iranian crude carriers on Saturday after Iran tried to attack a US aircraft carrier and a guided missile destroyer, according to CENTCOM.
"All IRGC attempts against US Navy warships have failed," it added.
Earlier Tuesday, the chief of staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, Ali Abdollahi, had warned that Tehran would attack US bases in the region if Iranian oil tankers were hit.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio however said Washington would continue to strike them in response to Iranian attacks.
"Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers," Rubio told reporters on a visit to Colombia.
Iran said it would target tankers off US allies Kuwait and Bahrain in response to Tuesday's US strikes.
"We warn all oil tankers in the Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports... whether they are anchored or docked -- we warn them to leave their vessels because they will be targeted," according to an IRGC statement posted eon the IRNA state news agency.
CENTCOM also said Tuesday that one of its underwater drones "malfunctioned," after Iran claimed its forces captured an American unmanned submarine in the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
"An underwater drone operated by US forces malfunctioned more than a day ago. It was surveying regional waters in support of ongoing operations," CENTCOM spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins said, without mentioning whether the device was seized by Iran.
"The defective drone was an older model that neither collected sensitive data nor carried any classified sonar or radar equipment," Hawkins added.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards had said they seized a US underwater drone at the "entrance to the Strait of Hormuz in a complex intelligence and operational action," describing it as "one of the most modern, unmanned, and smart submarines" operated by US forces.

item.title: Dhaka ranks third among world's most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked third among the world's most polluted cities on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 161 at 9:50 am.
The city's air quality was classified as 'unhealthy', meaning people may experience health effects due to elevated levels of air pollutants.
According to the AQI ranking, Malaysia's Kuching topped the list with a score of 184, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 179. Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, ranked fourth with an AQI of 158.
An AQI score between 101 and 150 is considered 'unhealthy for sensitive groups', while readings between 151 and 200 are classified as 'unhealthy'. Scores from 201 to 300 are considered 'very unhealthy', and readings above 301 are categorized as 'hazardous'.
The AQI is used to measure daily air quality and indicate the level of pollution in the atmosphere and its potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, air quality is assessed based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Afghanistan to host multi-format series against Bangladesh and Zimbabwe
item.description:
Afghanistan will host both Bangladesh and Zimbabwe across October and November in an extensive multi-format programme in the United Arab Emirates, featuring a one-off Test, an ODI Tri-Nation Series involving all three sides, and a three-match T20I series and two-match Test series against Zimbabwe.
Proceedings begin with the one-off Test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh from 9-13 October, before all three nations come together for the ODI Tri-Nation Series between 17 and 23 October.
Zimbabwe open their campaign against Bangladesh on 17 October, before facing hosts Afghanistan on 19 October. Afghanistan and Bangladesh then meet in the final league fixture on 21 October, with the top two sides progressing to the final on 23 October.
After the tri-series, Afghanistan and Zimbabwe switch to the shortest format for a three-match T20I series between 27 October and 1 November. The tour then concludes with a two-Test series between the two nations, running from 5-9 November and 13-17 November.
Afghanistan Cricket Board Chief Executive Officer Naseeb Khan welcomed the confirmation of the schedule.
"We are pleased to confirm this important period of international cricket for the Afghanistan National Team," he said. "Playing Bangladesh and Zimbabwe across different formats will provide our players with valuable competitive opportunities and offer our supporters an exciting period of international cricket.
Bangladesh Cricket Board Chief Executive Officer Nizam Uddin Chowdhury was similarly upbeat about the tour ahead, particularly the red-ball assignment.
"The Test match and the tri-nation series promise an exciting period of cricket for fans in both Bangladesh and Afghanistan," he said. "We attach great importance to Tests, and this will be an excellent opportunity for our players to experience red-ball cricket in the UAE for the first time and challenge themselves against a formidable Afghanistan side that has traditionally performed well in these conditions.

Three more die of dengue in Khulna division in 24 hours
item.description:
Three more people died of dengue in Khulna division in the past 24 hours, while 242 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the division.
The figures were disclosed in a report issued by the office of the Khulna divisional health director on Tuesday.
According to the report, a total of 7,660 dengue patients have been hospitalized in the division between January 1 and September 8 this year. Of them, 25 have died, while 6,578 have recovered and been discharged. Currently, 878 patients are receiving treatment at different hospitals, while 179 patients have been referred to other facilities.
Divisional Health Director Dr Sheikh Md Mosharraf Hossain said 206 of the 242 newly admitted patients were taken to government hospitals, while the remaining 36 were admitted to private hospitals.
Of the new patients, 97 were admitted in Khulna, including 61 at government hospitals and 36 at private facilities. Khulna Medical College Hospital reported 65 new admissions.
Meanwhile, 17 new patients were admitted in Bagerhat, 37 in Jessore, two in Jhenaidah, eight in Satkhira, five at Satkhira Medical College Hospital, two each in Magura and Narail, three each in Kushtia and Meherpur, and one in Chuadanga.
However, a rally and cleanliness drive were held in Khulna yesterday to raise public awareness about dengue prevention.
The Khulna Civil Surgeon’s Office organized the program, which began at the premises of Khulna 250-bed General Hospital.
Addressing the campaign, Deputy Commissioner Hure Jannat said there is no alternative to public awareness to prevent dengue and protect lives. “Everyone must remain aware and encourage others to take preventive measures,” she said, urging people not to panic over dengue fever and to care for patients according to doctors’ advice.
She also stressed the need for regular monitoring of surroundings, keeping homes and their adjacent areas clean, and using mosquito nets. The government alone cannot combat dengue, she said, urging people from all sections of society to play responsible roles.

item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8am on Tuesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 999.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 899, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 100, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the two new suspected fatalities, one was recorded in Sylhet and another in Barisal.
A total of 1,157 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Monday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 166,461.
During the same period, 79 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 19,835.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 146,359 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 140,850 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: 14,384 assistant teachers to join on October 1
item.description:
A total of 14,384 newly selected assistant teachers will join district primary education offices on October 1 and be posted to their respective schools three days later, Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon said on Tuesday.
The teachers were finally selected for appointment under the “Assistant Teacher Recruitment 2025” program, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj told Parliament on behalf of the education minister.
He made the disclosure in response to a question from lawmaker Md Selim Reza during the question-answer session of the third session of the 13th National Parliament.
Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal was in the chair.
Hajjaj said the 14,384 selected candidates will join the district primary education offices on October 1, 2026, before being posted to their respective schools on October 4.
Meanwhile, 36,960 posts of head teachers are currently vacant, the state minister said.
He said the process of filling the vacant posts through promotion of eligible teachers is underway following the disposal of Writ Petition No 73/2023 by the High Court Division of the Supreme Court.

item.title: Fraud conviction: Bidisha released on bail
item.description:
Bidisha Ershad, who was sentenced to two years in prison in a fraud case, was released on bail from Kashimpur Women’s Central Jail in Gazipur on Tuesday afternoon.
The former wife of former president Hussain Muhammad Ershad walked out of the jail around 5:15pm, Senior Jail Superintendent (additional charge) Md Nazrul Islam said.
“Bidisha’s bail documents reached the jail on Tuesday morning. After verifying the documents, she was released. She left the jail around 5:15pm,” he said.
The High Court granted Bidisha bail on Sunday after hearing a petition filed by her lawyer.
The bench of Justice Md Khairul Alam and Justice Md Rafizul Islam passed the order.
Bidisha was arrested around 8:30pm on August 25 from a restaurant in Gulshan, Dhaka, in the fraud case after a court sentenced her to two years in prison.
She was produced before a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court the following day. The court rejected her bail petition and ordered her to be sent to jail, where she remained until Tuesday.
On May 20, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court sentenced Bidisha to two years’ rigorous imprisonment in a case filed over allegations of fraud involving the sale of a flat.
The court also fined her Tk10,000, with one month’s imprisonment in default of payment.
As Bidisha was absent when the verdict was delivered, the court issued a warrant for her arrest to serve the sentence.
Bidisha appealed against the trial court’s verdict before the Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge’s Court and sought bail.
After hearing the petition, Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge Md Shahjahan Kabir rejected her bail application on September 2.
She subsequently moved the High Court challenging the order and seeking bail. She was later arrested and sent to jail.
